q: 'द रिपब्लिक' (The Republic) नामक कालजयी ग्रंथ के लेखक कौन हैं, जिसमें आदर्श राज्य और दार्शनिक राजा के सिद्धांत का प्रतिपादन किया गया है?
e: Plato (427–347 BCE) authored 'The Republic' (also titled 'Concerning Justice'), presenting his concept of the Ideal State ruled by Philosopher Kings (प्लेटो ने 'द रिपब्लिक' की रचना की, जिसमें आदर्श राज्य व दार्शनिक राजा का सिद्धांत है). Exam Boosters: (1) Plato founded 'The Academy' in Athens (387 BCE); (2) His other major works are 'The Statesman' and 'The Laws' (sub-ideal state ruled by law); (3) Plato divided society into 3 classes: Rulers (Reason), Auxiliaries/Soldiers (Spirit), and Producers (Appetite); (4) Karl Popper criticized Plato as an enemy of the 'Open Society'.
qe: Who is the author of the classical treatise 'The Republic', which outlines the theory of the Ideal State and the Philosopher King?

q: किस यूनानी दार्शनिक को 'राजनीति विज्ञान का जनक' कहा जाता है और जिन्होंने प्रसिद्ध कथन दिया कि "मनुष्य स्वभाव से एक राजनीतिक प्राणी है"?
e: Aristotle (384–322 BCE), author of 'Politics', is called the Father of Political Science and wrote "Man is by nature a political animal" (अरस्तू को राजनीति विज्ञान का जनक कहा जाता है). Exam Boosters: (1) Aristotle founded 'The Lyceum' in Athens and tutored Alexander the Great; (2) He studied 158 constitutions before writing 'Politics'; (3) He called Political Science the 'Master Science'; (4) His ethical principle of moderation is the 'Golden Mean' (स्वर्णिम मध्यमार्ग).
qe: Which Greek philosopher is universally known as the 'Father of Political Science' and famously stated that "Man is by nature a political animal"?

q: थॉमस हॉब्स ने अपनी पुस्तक 'लेवियाथन' (1651) में प्राकृतिक अवस्था में मानव जीवन का वर्णन किस प्रकार किया है?
o: Solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short
Guided by natural law and mutual consent
Free, equal, and led by the General Will
e: Hobbes depicted the State of Nature as a state of constant war of all against all, making life "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short" (एकाकी, दरिद्र, घृणित, पाशविक और अल्पायु). Exam Boosters: (1) To escape this anarchy, individuals surrender all rights (except self-preservation) to an absolute sovereign ('Leviathan'); (2) Hobbes's sovereign is NOT a party to the social contract; (3) His other works include 'De Cive' (1642) and 'Behemoth'; (4) Hobbes is regarded as the founder of modern absolutist sovereignty theory.
qe: In 'Leviathan' (1651), Thomas Hobbes described human life in the State of Nature as:
oe: Solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short
Guided by natural law and mutual consent
Free, equal, and led by the General Will

q: जॉन लॉक ने अपनी पुस्तक 'टू ट्रीटाइज़ेस ऑफ गवर्नमेंट' (1689) में किन तीन 'प्राकृतिक अधिकारों' को अविच्छेद्य और नागरिक समाज से पूर्व का माना है?
e: John Locke, the 'Father of Liberalism', identified Life, Liberty, and Property (जीवन, स्वतंत्रता और संपत्ति) as fundamental natural rights, with Property often encompassing all three. Exam Boosters: (1) Locke supported the Glorious Revolution of 1688 in England; (2) Unlike Hobbes, Locke advocated Limited Constitutional Government based on consent of the governed; (3) Locke proposed two contracts (social contract + political/trust contract) and the right to resist a tyrannical government; (4) His Labour Theory of Property states that mixing one's labour with nature creates private property.
qe: Which three 'Natural Rights' did John Locke consider inalienable and prior to the formation of civil society in his 'Two Treatises of Government' (1689)?

q: "मनुष्य स्वतंत्र पैदा होता है, किंतु सर्वत्र वह जंजीरों में जकड़ा हुआ है।" — यह प्रसिद्ध प्रारंभिक वाक्य किस राजनीतिक ग्रंथ का है?
o: The Social Contract — J. J. Rousseau
e: Jean-Jacques Rousseau opened 'The Social Contract' (1762) with this iconic statement (जीन-जैक रूसो की पुस्तक 'द सोशल कॉन्ट्रैक्ट' की प्रारंभिक पंक्ति). Exam Boosters: (1) Rousseau propounded the concept of 'General Will' (सामान्य इच्छा) and Popular Sovereignty; (2) He described early humans in the State of Nature as 'Noble Savages'; (3) His work inspired the French Revolution (1789); (4) His other famous works include 'Emile' (on education) and 'Discourse on the Origin of Inequality'.
qe: "Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains." — This famous opening line belongs to which political treatise?
oe: The Social Contract — J. J. Rousseau

q: "अधिकतम व्यक्तियों का अधिकतम सुख" के सूत्र द्वारा संक्षेपित शास्त्रीय उपयोगितावाद (Utilitarianism) के दर्शन का प्रतिपादन किसने किया?
e: Jeremy Bentham (1748–1832) founded Classical Utilitarianism in 'An Introduction to the Principles of Morals and Legislation' (1789) (जेरेमी बेंथम शास्त्रीय उपयोगितावाद के जनक हैं). Exam Boosters: (1) Bentham devised the 'Felicific Calculus' (सुखमापक यंत्र) to quantitatively measure pleasure and pain across 7 criteria; (2) He famously dismissed Natural Rights as "nonsense upon stilts"; (3) He designed the 'Panopticon' prison model; (4) Bentham stated "Pushpin is as good as poetry" if the quantity of pleasure is equal.
qe: Who propounded the philosophy of Classical Utilitarianism summarized by the formula "the greatest happiness of the greatest number"?

q: 'दास कैपिटल' (1867) और 'द कम्युनिस्ट मेनिफेस्टो' (1848, फ्रेडरिक एंगेल्स के साथ सह-लेखित) किसकी प्रमुख कृतियाँ हैं?
e: Karl Marx (1818–1883) authored 'Das Kapital' and co-authored 'The Communist Manifesto' (1848), laying the foundations of Scientific Socialism (कार्ल मार्क्स वैज्ञानिक समाजवाद के जनक हैं). Exam Boosters: (1) Marx borrowed Dialectics from Hegel and Materialism from Feuerbach to formulate Dialectical Materialism; (2) Key theories: Historical Materialism, Class Struggle, Theory of Surplus Value, and Alienation; (3) Famous quote: "Workers of the world, unite! You have nothing to lose but your chains"; (4) Marx envisioned a stateless, classless communist society after the 'withering away of the state'.
qe: 'Das Kapital' (1867) and 'The Communist Manifesto' (1848, co-authored with Friedrich Engels) are the seminal works of:

q: राज्यशास्त्र, अर्थव्यवस्था और कूटनीति पर कौटिल्य का कालजयी भारतीय ग्रंथ 'अर्थशास्त्र' कुल कितने अधिकरणों (अध्यायों) में विभाजित है?
e: Kautilya's (Chanakya/Vishnugupta) 'Arthashastra' consists of 15 Adhikaranas (Books) and 180 Prakaranas (कौटिल्य का अर्थशास्त्र 15 अधिकरणों में विभाजित है). Exam Boosters: (1) Discovered and published in 1909 by R. Shamasastry in Mysore; (2) Kautilya is often compared to Niccolò Machiavelli ('The Prince') for political realism; (3) Its 6th Adhikarana details the Saptanga Theory and Mandala Theory; (4) Kautilya defined 'Artha' as material livelihood and the territory inhabited by humans.
qe: Kautilya's 'Arthashastra', a classical Indian treatise on statecraft, economy, and diplomacy, is divided into how many Adhikaranas (Books)?

q: किस प्राचीन भारतीय विधि-निर्माता ने 'मनुस्मृति' की रचना की, जिसमें राजधर्म और राजत्व के दैवीय उत्पत्ति सिद्धांत का वर्णन है?
e: 'Manusmriti' (Manava Dharmashastra, 12 chapters) is attributed to Manu; its 7th chapter deals extensively with Rajdharma, kingship, Danda (punishment), and state administration (मनुस्मृति के 7वें अध्याय में राजधर्म का वर्णन है). Exam Boosters: (1) Manu stated that God created the King out of eternal particles of eight deities (Ashta-Lokapala: Indra, Vayu, Yama, Surya, Agni, Varuna, Chandra, Kubera); (2) Like Kautilya, Manu also described the 7 limbs (Saptanga) of the State; (3) Manu emphasized 'Danda' (coercive authority) as essential to prevent 'Matsyanyaya' (law of the fishes).
qe: Which ancient Indian lawgiver authored 'Manusmriti', presenting the concepts of Rajdharma and the divine origin of kingship?

q: महात्मा गांधी का प्रसिद्ध राजनीतिक घोषणापत्र 'हिंद स्वराज' (1909) मूल रूप से एसएस किल्डोनन कैसल जहाज पर किस भाषा में लिखा गया था?
e: Mahatma Gandhi wrote 'Hind Swaraj' in Gujarati in 1909 in dialogue form (between Editor and Reader) and later translated it into English himself (हिंद स्वराज मूलतः गुजराती भाषा में लिखा गया था). Exam Boosters: (1) In 'Hind Swaraj', Gandhi critiqued modern Western industrial civilization and parliamentary democracy; (2) He defined true 'Swaraj' as self-rule and self-control, not merely replacing British rulers with Indian rulers; (3) Gandhi's concept of 'Sarvodaya' (welfare of all) was inspired by John Ruskin's 'Unto This Last'; (4) Gandhi was also deeply influenced by Leo Tolstoy ('The Kingdom of God is Within You') and Henry David Thoreau ('Civil Disobedience').
qe: Mahatma Gandhi's famous political manifesto 'Hind Swaraj' (1909) was originally written in which language aboard the ship SS Kildonan Castle?

q: प्लेटो की 'रिपब्लिक' में किन वर्गों पर 'संपत्ति और पत्नियों का साम्यवाद' (निजी संपत्ति व परिवार का उन्मूलन) लागू किया गया है?
o: All three classes of the Ideal State equally
e: Plato restricted Communism of Property and Wives strictly to the Guardian class (Philosopher Rulers + Auxiliaries/Soldiers) to keep them free from economic greed and nepotism, while the Producer class retained private property and family (प्लेटो का साम्यवाद केवल अभिभावक वर्ग — शासक व सैनिक — पर लागू है). Exam Boosters: (1) Hence Plato's communism is called 'Half-Communism' or 'Aristocratic Communism', unlike Marx's communism for all; (2) Aristotle severely criticized Plato's communism of wives and property in 'Politics', arguing that "what is common to the greatest number has the least care bestowed upon it"; (3) Plato's Justice means each class performing its own allotted duty without interfering in others' spheres ('functional specialization').
qe: In Plato's 'Republic', which classes are subjected to the 'Communism of Property and Wives' (abolition of private property and private family)?
oe: All three classes of the Ideal State equally

q: अरस्तू के 'पॉलिटिक्स' में संविधानों के छह-स्तरीय वर्गीकरण में 'बहुतों के शासन' के शुद्ध (सामान्य) और विकृत रूप क्रमशः कौन-से हैं?
e: In Aristotle's classification: Rule of One → Monarchy (pure) / Tyranny (perverted); Rule of Few → Aristocracy (pure) / Oligarchy (perverted); Rule of Many → Polity (pure, constitutional government by middle class) / Democracy (perverted, mob rule by poor) (बहुतों का शुद्ध शासन 'पॉलिटी' और विकृत रूप 'लोकतंत्र/डेमोक्रेसी' है). Exam Boosters: (1) Aristotle considered 'Polity' (संवैधानिक तंत्र) as the best practicable state based on his Golden Mean; (2) Aristotle excluded women, slaves, artisans, and resident aliens from citizenship, defining a citizen as one who participates in judicial and deliberative offices.
qe: In Aristotle's six-fold classification of constitutions in 'Politics', what are the pure (normal) and perverted forms of the 'Rule of the Many' respectively?

q: जीन-जैक रूसो की 'सामान्य इच्छा' (General Will) की अवधारणा के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
o: General Will is identical to the 'Will of All' (sum of private wills).
General Will is inalienable, indivisible, and infallible.
General Will always aims at the common good of society.
Rousseau remarked that anyone refusing to obey the General Will shall be "forced to be free".
e: Rousseau strictly distinguished 'General Will' (sum of 'real wills' aiming at common good) from the 'Will of All' (sum of selfish 'actual wills') — they are NOT identical (सामान्य इच्छा और सबकी इच्छा एक समान नहीं हैं). Exam Boosters: (1) General Will represents Popular Sovereignty; (2) Rousseau rejected representative democracy in favour of direct democracy (as in ancient Greek city-states and Geneva); (3) Because of "forced to be free", critics like Jacob Talmon called Rousseau a precursor of 'Totalitarian Democracy'.
qe: Which of the following statements regarding Jean-Jacques Rousseau's concept of 'General Will' (Volonté Générale) is NOT correct?
oe: General Will is identical to the 'Will of All' (sum of private wills).
General Will is inalienable, indivisible, and infallible.
General Will always aims at the common good of society.
Rousseau remarked that anyone refusing to obey the General Will shall be "forced to be free".

q: जॉन स्टुअर्ट मिल ने अपने निबंध 'यूटिलिटेरियनिज़्म' (1861) में जेरेमी बेंथम के शास्त्रीय उपयोगितावाद में क्या प्रमुख संशोधन किया?
o: He introduced a qualitative distinction between higher (intellectual) and lower (sensual) pleasures.
He rejected the concept of pleasure completely.
He argued that the State should control all private religious beliefs.
He proposed abolishing representative democracy in favour of monarchy.
e: Unlike Bentham who measured pleasure only quantitatively, J. S. Mill introduced QUALITATIVE differences among pleasures, famously declaring: "It is better to be a human being dissatisfied than a pig satisfied; better to be Socrates dissatisfied than a fool satisfied" (मिल ने सुखों में गुणात्मक अंतर प्रस्तुत किया). Exam Boosters: (1) Mill is called the 'Reluctant Democrat' because he feared 'Tyranny of the Majority' and proposed Plural Voting (extra votes for educated citizens); (2) Mill championed women's suffrage in 'The Subjection of Women' (1869); (3) C. L. Wayper called Mill "the last of the utilitarians and the foremost of the individualists".
qe: How did John Stuart Mill modify Jeremy Bentham's Classical Utilitarianism in his essay 'Utilitarianism' (1861)?
oe: He introduced a qualitative distinction between higher (intellectual) and lower (sensual) pleasures.
He rejected the concept of pleasure completely.
He argued that the State should control all private religious beliefs.
He proposed abolishing representative democracy in favour of monarchy.

q: 'ऑन लिबर्टी' (1859) में जे. एस. मिल ने राज्य के हस्तक्षेप की वैध सीमा तय करने हेतु मानव कार्यों को किन दो श्रेणियों में विभाजित किया?
e: Under Mill's 'Harm Principle', the state has NO right to interfere in 'Self-regarding actions' (स्व-संबंधी कार्य — affecting only the individual), and may intervene only in 'Other-regarding actions' (पर-संबंधी कार्य) to prevent harm to others. Exam Boosters: (1) Mill wrote: "Over himself, over his own body and mind, the individual is sovereign"; (2) Mill strongly defended absolute freedom of thought and expression; (3) In 'Considerations on Representative Government' (1861), Mill supported Hare's system of Proportional Representation and Open Ballot.
qe: In 'On Liberty' (1859), J. S. Mill divided human actions into two categories to define the legitimate limit of state interference. What are they?

q: कार्ल मार्क्स के 'अतिरिक्त मूल्य के सिद्धांत' (Theory of Surplus Value) में अतिरिक्त मूल्य से क्या तात्पर्य है?
o: The tax collected by the capitalist state on luxury imports
The interest earned by banks on agricultural loans
The difference between the value created by a worker's labour and the wages paid to the worker
The excess money printed by central banks causing inflation
e: Surplus value (अतिरिक्त मूल्य) is the unpaid labour value appropriated by the capitalist — the difference between the total exchange value produced by the worker and the subsistence wage paid to the worker. Exam Boosters: (1) Marx's 'Historical Materialism' divides society into Economic Base (forces & relations of production) and Superstructure (law, politics, religion, ideology); (2) Stages of history according to Marx: Primitive Communism → Slavery → Feudalism → Capitalism → Socialism (Dictatorship of Proletariat) → Communism; (3) 'Alienation' (अलगाव) was elaborated in Marx's 'Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844'.
qe: In Karl Marx's 'Theory of Surplus Value', surplus value refers to:
oe: The tax collected by the capitalist state on luxury imports
The interest earned by banks on agricultural loans
The difference between the value created by a worker's labour and the wages paid to the worker
The excess money printed by central banks causing inflation

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कौटिल्य के 'सप्तांग सिद्धांत' के अंतर्गत राज्य के सात अंगों (प्रकृतियों) में शामिल नहीं है?
e: The 7 limbs (Saptanga) in Kautilya's Arthashastra are: (1) Swami (King), (2) Amatya (Minister), (3) Janapada (Territory & Population), (4) Durga (Fort), (5) Kosha (Treasury), (6) Danda/Bala (Army/Justice), and (7) Mitra (Ally). 'Purohita' is NOT one of the seven limbs (पुरोहित सप्तांग में शामिल नहीं है). Exam Boosters: (1) Kautilya placed 'Swami' at the head of the organic state; (2) In Kautilya's Mandala Theory (circle of 12 kings), the ambitious central king is called 'Vijigishu' (विजिगीषु — desirer of conquest); (3) Immediate neighbour of Vijigishu is 'Ari' (enemy), and neighbour's neighbour is 'Mitra' (friend).
qe: Which of the following is NOT one of the seven elements (Prakritis) of the State in Kautilya's 'Saptanga Theory'?

q: महात्मा गांधी के सामाजिक-आर्थिक 'न्यासिता सिद्धांत' (Trusteeship) का मूल विचार क्या है?
o: Violent confiscation of all private wealth by the State
Wealthy owners should retain only what they need and hold surplus wealth as trustees for society's welfare
Complete abolition of agriculture in favour of heavy mechanization
Handing over all private industries to foreign multinational trusts
e: Gandhi's Trusteeship proposes non-violent economic transformation where capitalists/landlords voluntarily consider themselves trustees of surplus wealth for the benefit of the poor, avoiding violent class war (अमीर वर्ग अतिरिक्त संपत्ति को समाज के कल्याण हेतु न्यासी के रूप में रखे). Exam Boosters: (1) Inspired by the opening verse of 'Ishopanishad' ("Tena tyaktena bhunjitha"); (2) Gandhi's political ideal was 'Ram Rajya' — a stateless, non-violent democracy based on decentralized village republics ('Oceanic Circle'); (3) Gandhi's 'Talisman' asks decision-makers to recall the face of the poorest and weakest person.
qe: What is the core idea of Mahatma Gandhi's socio-economic 'Theory of Trusteeship' (न्यासिता सिद्धांत)?
oe: Violent confiscation of all private wealth by the State
Wealthy owners should retain only what they need and hold surplus wealth as trustees for society's welfare
Complete abolition of agriculture in favour of heavy mechanization
Handing over all private industries to foreign multinational trusts

q:
निम्नलिखित राजनीतिक विचारकों को उनकी प्रसिद्ध पुस्तकों से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. थॉमस हॉब्स — (a) टू ट्रीटाइज़ेस ऑफ गवर्नमेंट
2. जॉन लॉक — (b) लेवियाथन
3. जे. एस. मिल — (c) कंसिडरेशंस ऑन रिप्रेजेंटेटिव गवर्नमेंट
4. जेरेमी बेंथम — (d) फ्रेगमेंट ऑन गवर्नमेंट
e: Hobbes — Leviathan (1651); Locke — Two Treatises of Government (1689); J. S. Mill — Considerations on Representative Government (1861); Bentham — A Fragment on Government (1776). Correct match: 1-b, 2-a, 3-c, 4-d (सही मिलान 1-b, 2-a, 3-c, 4-d है).
qe:
Match the following Political Thinkers with their famous books:
1. Thomas Hobbes — (a) Two Treatises of Government
2. John Locke — (b) Leviathan
3. J. S. Mill — (c) Considerations on Representative Government
4. Jeremy Bentham — (d) Fragment on Government

q: कौटिल्य की 'षाड्गुण्य' (छह-सूत्रीय विदेश नीति) में 'द्वैधीभाव' का क्या अर्थ है?
o: Making permanent peace with all neighbouring kingdoms
Seeking shelter under a stronger king when weak
Remaining completely neutral during a regional conflict
Adopting a dual policy — making peace with one neighbour while waging war against another
e: The 6 policies (Shadgunya) are: (1) Sandhi (peace/alliance), (2) Vigraha (war), (3) Asana (neutrality/waiting), (4) Yana (marching/preparedness), (5) Samshraya (seeking shelter of a stronger king), and (6) Dvaidhibhava (dual policy — peace with one, war with another) (द्वैधीभाव = एक से संधि और दूसरे से युद्ध). Exam Boosters: (1) Kautilya also prescribed four Upayas (methods of diplomacy): Sama (conciliation), Dana (gifts), Bheda (dissension), and Danda (force).
qe: In Kautilya's 'Shadgunya' (Six-fold Foreign Policy), what does 'Dvaidhibhava' (द्वैधीभाव) mean?
oe: Making permanent peace with all neighbouring kingdoms
Seeking shelter under a stronger king when weak
Remaining completely neutral during a regional conflict
Adopting a dual policy — making peace with one neighbour while waging war against another

q: अरस्तू ने अपनी कृति 'निकोमैशियन एथिक्स' और 'पॉलिटिक्स' में न्याय के किन दो प्रमुख रूपों में भेद किया है?
e: Aristotle divided Particular Justice into: (1) Distributive Justice (वितरणात्मक न्याय — honours/offices distributed proportionately according to merit/desert) and (2) Corrective/Commutative Justice (संशोधनात्मक न्याय — restoring arithmetic equality in transactions and crimes). Exam Boosters: (1) Aristotle's famous quote on inequality: "Treat equals equally and unequals unequally"; (2) For Aristotle, the State exists not merely for life, "it comes into existence for the sake of life and continues to exist for the sake of the good life".
qe: Aristotle distinguished between two forms of Justice in his 'Nicomachean Ethics' and 'Politics'. What are they?

q: किस विचारक ने प्रसिद्ध कथन दिया कि "संप्रभुता नागरिकों और प्रजाजनों के ऊपर विधि द्वारा अनियंत्रित सर्वोच्च शक्ति है", जिसे बाद में हॉब्स ने पूर्ण विधिक निरंकुशता प्रदान की?
e: French thinker Jean Bodin ('Six Books of the Commonwealth', 1576) first systematically defined Sovereignty, though he kept it bound by divine and natural laws; Thomas Hobbes removed even those limits to make Sovereignty absolute and indivisible (जीन बोदाँ ने संप्रभुता की प्रथम व्यवस्थित परिभाषा दी). Exam Boosters: (1) John Austin ('Lectures on Jurisprudence', 1832) gave the Legal/Monistic Theory of Sovereignty; (2) Harold Laski and R. M. MacIver championed the Pluralist Theory of Sovereignty.
qe: Which thinker famously remarked that "Sovereignty is the supreme power over citizens and subjects, unrestrained by law", while Hobbes later gave it full legal absolutism?

q: महात्मा गांधी ने स्वयं को "दार्शनिक अराजकतावादी" (Philosophical Anarchist) मुख्यतः इसलिए कहा क्योंकि उनका मानना था कि:
o: Society should have no moral rules or ethical discipline.
The State represents concentrated violence, so an ideal non-violent society would be stateless and self-regulated.
All democratic constitutions must be overthrown by armed revolt.
Only hereditary monarchs can maintain social order.
e: Gandhi viewed the State as a 'soulless machine' representing violence in a concentrated form; his ideal 'Enlightened Anarchy' (Ram Rajya) is a stateless, self-regulated society of moral individuals (गांधीजी राज्य को हिंसा का केंद्रित रूप मानते थे और आदर्श समाज को राज्यविहीन स्व-शासित समाज मानते थे). Exam Boosters: (1) Gandhi insisted on purity of both 'Means and Ends' ("As the means, so the end"); (2) His 11 Vows (Ekadasha Vrata) include Satya, Ahimsa, Asteya, Brahmacharya, Aparigraha, and Swadeshi.
qe: Mahatma Gandhi described himself as a "Philosophical Anarchist" primarily because he believed:
oe: Society should have no moral rules or ethical discipline.
The State represents concentrated violence, so an ideal non-violent society would be stateless and self-regulated.
All democratic constitutions must be overthrown by armed revolt.
Only hereditary monarchs can maintain social order.

q:
'द रिपब्लिक' में प्लेटो के शिक्षा सिद्धांत के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: प्लेटो की शिक्षा योजना राज्य-नियंत्रित है और अभिभावक वर्ग के पुरुषों तथा महिलाओं दोनों के लिए समान रूप से खुली है।
कथन II: प्लेटो के पाठ्यक्रम में द्वंद्वशास्त्र (दर्शन) का अध्ययन 30 वर्ष की आयु में प्रारंभ होता है और 50 वर्ष की आयु में दार्शनिक राजा बनने से पूर्व व्यावहारिक शासन का प्रशिक्षण होता है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
e: Both statements are correct. Rousseau hailed Plato's 'Republic' as "the finest treatise on education ever written" — Plato proposed equal education for women, music+gymnastics up to 20, mathematics 20–30, dialectics 30–35, practical administration 35–50, and Philosopher King at 50 (दोनों कथन सही हैं).
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding Plato's Theory of Education in 'The Republic':
Statement I: Plato's educational scheme is state-controlled and open equally to both men and women of the Guardian class.
Statement II: In Plato's curriculum, the study of Dialectics (Philosophy) begins at age 30 and culminates in practical governance before attaining Philosopher King status at age 50.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q:
'पॉलिटिक्स' के पाँचवें खंड में अरस्तू के क्रांति सिद्धांत के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: अरस्तू ने समानता की आकांक्षा (असमानता व अन्याय की अनुभूति) को क्रांतियों का सार्वभौमिक मूल कारण माना।
कथन II: अरस्तू के अनुसार, संविधान में शांतिपूर्ण परिवर्तन (जैसे कुलीनतंत्र से अल्पतंत्र) भी क्रांति कहलाता है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
e: Both statements are correct. For Aristotle, any change in the constitution or ruling personnel (whether violent or peaceful) is a revolution, rooted primarily in perceived inequality (दोनों कथन सही हैं). Exam Boosters: (1) To prevent revolutions, Aristotle advocated strengthening the Middle Class, upholding the Rule of Law, and educating citizens in the spirit of the constitution; (2) Aristotle defended Slavery as natural (in Book I of 'Politics') — a major critique against him.
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding Aristotle's Theory of Revolution in Book V of 'Politics':
Statement I: Aristotle identified the passion for equality (perceived inequality and injustice) as the universal root cause of revolutions.
Statement II: According to Aristotle, even a peaceful change in the constitution (e.g., from aristocracy to oligarchy) constitutes a revolution.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q: निम्नलिखित में से राजनीतिक विचारक और उनके प्रसिद्ध कथन का कौन-सा युग्म सही सुमेलित नहीं है?
o: Thomas Hobbes — "Covenants, without the sword, are but words."
John Locke — "Where there is no law, there is no freedom."
J. S. Mill — "The worth of a State, in the long run, is the worth of the individuals composing it."
Karl Marx — "The state is the march of God on earth."
e: "The state is the march of God on earth" was stated by G. W. F. Hegel (Idealism), NOT Karl Marx! Marx called the state "a committee for managing the common affairs of the whole bourgeoisie" ("राज्य पृथ्वी पर ईश्वर का अवतरण है" हेगेल का कथन है, मार्क्स का नहीं). Exam Boosters: (1) Hobbes: "Covenants without the sword are but words"; (2) Locke: "Where there is no law, there is no freedom"; (3) Marx: "Religion is the opium of the people".
qe: Which of the following pairs of Political Thinker and famous quotation is NOT correctly matched?
oe: Thomas Hobbes — "Covenants, without the sword, are but words."
John Locke — "Where there is no law, there is no freedom."
J. S. Mill — "The worth of a State, in the long run, is the worth of the individuals composing it."
Karl Marx — "The state is the march of God on earth."

q: सामाजिक अनुबंध की प्रकृति पर हॉब्स, लॉक और रूसो की तुलना कीजिए। निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सटीक है?
o: In Hobbes, sovereignty is absolute and vested in a ruler outside the contract; in Locke, limited and fiduciary; in Rousseau, absolute and vested in the community's General Will.
In Hobbes, individuals surrender rights to the community as a whole; in Rousseau, to a third-party monarch.
All three thinkers viewed the State of Nature as a brutal war of all against all.
All three thinkers rejected the right to private property.
e: Option A accurately summarizes the three social contractarians: Hobbes (absolute sovereignty to an external Leviathan), Locke (limited constitutional government as a fiduciary trust), and Rousseau (absolute popular sovereignty vested in the General Will of the community itself) (विकल्प A तीनों संविदावादियों का सही अंतर दर्शाता है). Exam Boosters: (1) In Locke, the State of Nature is pre-political (peaceful, governed by natural law) but inconvenient due to lack of impartial judge, known law, and executive power; (2) Rousseau said: "Hobbes's sovereign is headless" — actually, Vaughan remarked that Rousseau's Leviathan is Hobbes's Leviathan with its head chopped off!
qe: Compare Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau on the nature of the Social Contract. Which of the following statements is accurate?
oe: In Hobbes, sovereignty is absolute and vested in a ruler outside the contract; in Locke, limited and fiduciary; in Rousseau, absolute and vested in the community's General Will.
In Hobbes, individuals surrender rights to the community as a whole; in Rousseau, to a third-party monarch.
All three thinkers viewed the State of Nature as a brutal war of all against all.
All three thinkers rejected the right to private property.

q: कौटिल्य के अंतर्राज्यीय संबंधों के 'मंडल सिद्धांत' में 'मध्यम' और 'उदासीन' राज्यों की क्या भूमिकाएँ हैं?
o: Both are vassal states permanently annexed by the Vijigishu.
Both refer to internal spy networks inside the capital city.
Madhyama is the rear enemy and Udasina is the rear friend.
Madhyama borders both Vijigishu and Ari and can aid/resist either; Udasina lies outside their circle and is powerful enough to remain neutral.
e: In the 12-state Mandala circle: Madhyama (मध्यम) shares borders with both Vijigishu and Ari and is capable of helping or opposing either; Udasina (उदासीन) is a powerful detached/neutral state outside the immediate conflict zone (मध्यम दोनों का सीमावर्ती व सक्षम राज्य तथा उदासीन मंडल से बाहर स्थित शक्तिशाली तटस्थ राज्य है). Exam Boosters: (1) Rear enemy is called 'Parshnigraha' (पार्ष्णिग्राह) and rear friend is 'Akranda' (आक्रन्द); (2) Total states in the Mandala = 12 (1 Vijigishu + 5 in front + 4 in rear + 1 Madhyama + 1 Udasina).
qe: In Kautilya's 'Mandala Theory' of inter-state relations, what are the roles of 'Madhyama' (मध्यम) and 'Udasina' (उदासीन) states?
oe: Both are vassal states permanently annexed by the Vijigishu.
Both refer to internal spy networks inside the capital city.
Madhyama is the rear enemy and Udasina is the rear friend.
Madhyama borders both Vijigishu and Ari and can aid/resist either; Udasina lies outside their circle and is powerful enough to remain neutral.

q:
मनु की 'मनुस्मृति' और कौटिल्य के 'अर्थशास्त्र' के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: मनु धर्म को राजनीति से सर्वथा ऊपर रखते हैं और राजत्व को दैवीय उत्पत्ति मानते हैं।
कथन II: कौटिल्य राजनीति को धर्मशास्त्र से अपेक्षाकृत पृथक कर यथार्थवादी दृष्टिकोण अपनाते हैं जहाँ राजशासन का सर्वोच्च प्रशासनिक महत्व है।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
e: Both statements are correct. While Manu represents the Dharmashastra tradition (divine origin of kingship), Kautilya represents the Arthashastra tradition (pragmatic realism and quasi-contractual origin of state to end Matsyanyaya) (दोनों कथन सही हैं).
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding Manu's 'Manusmriti' and Kautilya's 'Arthashastra':
Statement I: Manu places Dharma (moral-sacred law) strictly above politics and views kingship as divinely ordained.
Statement II: Kautilya separates politics from theology to a greater extent, adopting a pragmatic realist approach where the King's decree (Rajasasana) holds supreme administrative force.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी कृति कार्ल मार्क्स (अकेले या एंगेल्स के साथ) द्वारा नहीं लिखी गई है?
e: 'The Philosophy of Poverty' (1846) was written by French anarchist Pierre-Joseph Proudhon; Karl Marx wrote 'The Poverty of Philosophy' (1847) as a scathing rebuttal to Proudhon! ('द फिलॉसफी ऑफ पॉवर्टी' प्रूधों की कृति है, मार्क्स ने इसके उत्तर में 'द पॉवर्टी ऑफ फिलॉसफी' लिखी). Exam Boosters: (1) Proudhon famously declared "Property is theft"; (2) Marx's 'The German Ideology' (1845) systematically outlines Historical Materialism.
qe: Which of the following works was NOT written by Karl Marx (alone or with Engels)?

q: 'कंसिडरेशंस ऑन रिप्रेजेंटेटिव गवर्नमेंट' में जे. एस. मिल ने 'बहुल मतदान' (उच्च शिक्षित नागरिकों को अतिरिक्त मत) की वकालत क्यों की?
o: To ensure that property-less workers could never vote
To prevent the numerical majority of uneducated voters from overshadowing educated and minority opinion
To abolish Parliament and establish rule by philosophers
To replace universal adult suffrage with hereditary aristocracy
e: Mill supported universal suffrage (including women) subject to literacy/tax qualification, but feared 'tyranny of the majority' (class legislation by an uneducated majority), so he proposed Plural Voting to give intellectual merit greater weight (शिक्षित व अल्पसंख्यक मत को बहुमत की निरंकुशता से बचाने हेतु). Exam Boosters: (1) Mill also favoured Hare's Proportional Representation so minorities get fair parliamentary representation; (2) Mill opposed the Secret Ballot, arguing voting is a public trust to be exercised openly.
qe: Why did J. S. Mill advocate 'Plural Voting' (giving additional votes to citizens with higher education or mental qualifications) in 'Considerations on Representative Government'?
oe: To ensure that property-less workers could never vote
To prevent the numerical majority of uneducated voters from overshadowing educated and minority opinion
To abolish Parliament and establish rule by philosophers
To replace universal adult suffrage with hereditary aristocracy

q: गांधीवादी राजनीतिक चिंतन में 'सत्याग्रह' और 'निष्क्रिय प्रतिरोध' (Passive Resistance) के बीच सटीक अंतर क्या है?
o: Satyagraha is based on love, truth, and complete non-violence (weapon of the strong) aiming to convert the opponent's heart, whereas Passive Resistance is tactical and does not rule out hatred or force if opportune.
Satyagraha is a weapon of the weak, while Passive Resistance is a weapon of the strong.
Both terms are completely synonymous in Gandhi's writings.
Passive Resistance is purely spiritual, whereas Satyagraha is an armed rebellion.
e: Gandhi clearly distinguished them in 'Satyagraha in South Africa': Satyagraha is the 'weapon of the strong' rooted in soul-force (Atmabala), Ahimsa, and love to transform the opponent, whereas Passive Resistance is often a tactical weapon of the weak that may harbour ill-will (सत्याग्रह सबल का अस्त्र है जो प्रेम व अहिंसा से विरोधी का हृदय परिवर्तन करता है).
qe: In Gandhian political thought, what is the precise distinction between 'Satyagraha' and 'Passive Resistance'?
oe: Satyagraha is based on love, truth, and complete non-violence (weapon of the strong) aiming to convert the opponent's heart, whereas Passive Resistance is tactical and does not rule out hatred or force if opportune.
Satyagraha is a weapon of the weak, while Passive Resistance is a weapon of the strong.
Both terms are completely synonymous in Gandhi's writings.
Passive Resistance is purely spiritual, whereas Satyagraha is an armed rebellion.

q: सामाजिक और राष्ट्रीय सेवा के लिए समर्पित कार्यकर्ताओं को प्रशिक्षित करने हेतु 1905 में पुणे में 'सर्वेंट्स ऑफ इंडिया सोसाइटी' की स्थापना किसने की थी?
e: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society on 12 June 1905 in Pune (गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले ने 1905 में सर्वेंट्स ऑफ इंडिया सोसाइटी की स्थापना की). Exam Boosters: (1) Gokhale is regarded as the Political Guru of Mahatma Gandhi (and M. G. Ranade was Gokhale's political guru); (2) Gokhale presided over the 1905 Banaras Session of the INC; (3) He championed the 'Spiritualization of Politics' and constitutional moderation; (4) He published the English weekly 'Hitavada'.
qe: Who founded the 'Servants of India Society' in Pune in 1905 to train dedicated missionaries for social and national service?

q: "स्वराज्य मेरा जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार है और मैं इसे लेकर रहूँगा" — यह प्रसिद्ध राष्ट्रवादी उद्घोष किसने किया था?
e: Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak popularized this slogan (especially during the 1916 Home Rule Movement and Lucknow Congress) (बाल गंगाधर तिलक ने यह प्रसिद्ध नारा दिया). Exam Boosters: (1) Valentine Chirol called Tilak the "Father of Indian Unrest" (in his book 'Indian Unrest'); (2) Tilak started the Ganapati Festival (1893) and Shivaji Festival (1895) to foster mass nationalism; (3) Tilak was part of the Extremist trio 'Lal-Bal-Pal'; (4) Tilak founded the Indian Home Rule League in April 1916 (before Annie Besant's League in Sept 1916).
qe: Who declared the iconic nationalist slogan "Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it" (स्वराज्य मेरा जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार है और मैं इसे लेकर रहूँगा)?

q: 'द डिस्कवरी ऑफ इंडिया' (भारत एक खोज — 1942–45 में अहमदनगर किले में कारावास के दौरान लिखित) के लेखक कौन हैं?
e: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' (published 1946) while imprisoned at Ahmednagar Fort during the Quit India Movement (जवाहरलाल नेहरू ने 'डिस्कवरी ऑफ इंडिया' लिखी). Exam Boosters: (1) Nehru's other notable books: 'Glimpses of World History' and 'An Autobiography (Toward Freedom)'; (2) Nehru presided over the 1929 Lahore Session of INC where the 'Purna Swaraj' resolution was passed; (3) He was the principal architect of India's Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) and Democratic Socialism.
qe: Who authored 'The Discovery of India' (written during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar Fort in 1942–45)?

q: 1939 में त्रिपुरी संकट के बाद कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष पद से त्यागपत्र देकर सुभाष चंद्र बोस ने किस राजनीतिक दल की स्थापना की थी?
e: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose founded the All India Forward Bloc on 3 May 1939 within the Congress framework to unite radical left-wing nationalist forces (सुभाष चंद्र बोस ने 1939 में फॉरवर्ड ब्लॉक की स्थापना की). Exam Boosters: (1) Bose presided over the Haripura Session (1938) and won the Tripuri Session (1939) election defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya; (2) He wrote 'The Indian Struggle'; (3) His political guru was Deshbandhu Chittaranjan Das; (4) He was the first to address Mahatma Gandhi as 'Father of the Nation' (July 1944, Azad Hind Radio).
qe: After resigning as Congress President following the Tripuri Crisis in 1939, Subhas Chandra Bose founded which political party?

q: 'एनाहिलेशन ऑफ कास्ट' (जाति का विनाश, 1936) के लेखक और भारतीय संविधान की प्रारूप समिति के अध्यक्ष कौन थे?
e: Dr. Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar authored 'Annihilation of Caste' (1936) and chaired the 7-member Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly (डॉ. बी. आर. आंबेडकर प्रारूप समिति के अध्यक्ष और 'एनाहिलेशन ऑफ कास्ट' के लेखक थे). Exam Boosters: (1) Founded Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha (1924) and Independent Labour Party (1936); (2) Published newspapers 'Mooknayak' (1920) and 'Bahishkrit Bharat'; (3) Led the Mahad Satyagraha (1927) for access to public water; (4) Participated in all three Round Table Conferences (1930–32).
qe: Who authored the seminal treatise 'Annihilation of Caste' (1936) and chaired the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution?

q: बाल गंगाधर तिलक ने दो प्रसिद्ध राष्ट्रवादी समाचारपत्रों 'केसरी' और 'मराठा' का संपादन किया। ये क्रमशः किन भाषाओं में प्रकाशित होते थे?
e: 'Kesari' was published in Marathi and 'Mahratta' in English (started in 1881 with Gopal Ganesh Agarkar) ('केसरी' मराठी में तथा 'मराठा' अंग्रेजी में प्रकाशित होता था). Exam Boosters: (1) Tilak wrote 'Gita Rahasya' (stressing Karma Yoga) during his 6-year imprisonment in Mandalay Jail (Burma, 1908–14); (2) He also authored 'The Arctic Home in the Vedas' and 'Orion'; (3) Tilak was tried for sedition thrice (1897, 1908, 1916).
qe: Bal Gangadhar Tilak edited two famous nationalist newspapers — 'Kesari' and 'Mahratta'. In which languages were they published respectively?

q: मुहम्मद अली जिन्ना के राजनीतिक जीवन के प्रारंभिक चरण (1916 के लखनऊ समझौते के समय) में किसने उन्हें "हिंदू-मुस्लिम एकता का राजदूत" कहा था?
e: Sarojini Naidu hailed Jinnah as the "Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity" (and edited a collection of his speeches under that title) following his key role in the 1916 Lucknow Pact (सरोजिनी नायडू ने जिन्ना को 'हिंदू-मुस्लिम एकता का राजदूत' कहा था). Exam Boosters: (1) Jinnah initially belonged to the INC and admired Gopal Krishna Gokhale; (2) In 1929, Jinnah presented his 'Fourteen Points' in response to the Nehru Report (1928); (3) The Muslim League passed the Lahore Resolution (Pakistan Resolution) under Jinnah's presidency in March 1940.
qe: Who famously hailed Muhammad Ali Jinnah in the early phase of his political career (around the 1916 Lucknow Pact) as the "Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity"?

q: अप्रैल 1954 में भारत (जवाहरलाल नेहरू) और चीन (चाउ एन-लाई) के बीच शांतिपूर्ण सह-अस्तित्व के पाँच सिद्धांत ('पंचशील') किस समझौते के अंतर्गत हस्ताक्षरित हुए?
o: Sino-Indian Agreement on Trade and Intercourse with Tibet
e: The Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence (Panchsheel) were first codified in the preamble of the Sino-Indian Agreement on Trade and Intercourse with Tibet signed on 29 April 1954 (29 अप्रैल 1954 को तिब्बत व्यापार समझौते के तहत पंचशील पर हस्ताक्षर हुए). Exam Boosters: (1) The 5 principles: Mutual respect for sovereignty/territorial integrity, Mutual non-aggression, Mutual non-interference in internal affairs, Equality and mutual benefit, Peaceful coexistence; (2) Panchsheel later formed the bedrock of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM, first summit at Belgrade in 1961 — Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Sukarno, Nkrumah).
qe: Which five principles of peaceful coexistence ('Panchsheel') were formally signed between India (Jawaharlal Nehru) and China (Zhou Enlai) in April 1954?
oe: Sino-Indian Agreement on Trade and Intercourse with Tibet

q:
निम्नलिखित राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन के नेताओं को उनके द्वारा संपादित/स्थापित समाचारपत्रों से सुमेलित कीजिए:
1. महात्मा गांधी — (a) मूकनायक
2. बाल गंगाधर तिलक — (b) यंग इंडिया एवं हरिजन
3. डॉ. बी. आर. आंबेडकर — (c) केसरी
4. जवाहरलाल नेहरू — (d) नेशनल हेराल्ड
e: Mahatma Gandhi — Young India, Navajivan, Harijan (and Indian Opinion in South Africa); Tilak — Kesari & Mahratta; Dr. Ambedkar — Mooknayak (1920); Jawaharlal Nehru — National Herald (1938, Lucknow). Correct match: 1-b, 2-c, 3-a, 4-d (सही मिलान 1-b, 2-c, 3-a, 4-d है).
qe:
Match the following National Movement Leaders with the newspapers/journals they edited or founded:
1. Mahatma Gandhi — (a) Mooknayak
2. Bal Gangadhar Tilak — (b) Young India & Harijan
3. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar — (c) Kesari
4. Jawaharlal Nehru — (d) National Herald

q:
भारत में महात्मा गांधी के तीन प्रारंभिक सत्याग्रह आंदोलनों को सही कालानुक्रम में व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
1. खेड़ा सत्याग्रह
2. चंपारण सत्याग्रह
3. अहमदाबाद मिल हड़ताल
e: Champaran Satyagraha (April 1917 — first Civil Disobedience against Tinkathia indigo system) → Ahmedabad Mill Strike (Feb–March 1918 — first Hunger Strike for 35% plague bonus) → Kheda Satyagraha (March–June 1918 — first Non-Cooperation for land revenue remission). Correct order: 2, 3, 1 (सही क्रम 2, 3, 1 है).
qe:
Arrange Mahatma Gandhi's three early Satyagraha movements in India in their correct chronological order:
1. Kheda Satyagraha
2. Champaran Satyagraha
3. Ahmedabad Mill Strike

q: गोपाल कृष्ण गोखले के संबंध में निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?
o: He testified before the Welby Commission (1897) in London on Indian public expenditure.
He introduced a bill in the Imperial Legislative Council in 1911 for free and compulsory elementary education.
He supported the Extremist demand for immediate boycott of all British institutions at Surat (1907).
He was elected President of the Indian National Congress at the 1905 Banaras Session.
e: Gokhale was the foremost leader of the MODERATE wing of the Congress and strongly opposed the Extremist boycott-all-institutions strategy at Surat (1907), favouring constitutional agitation (गोखले उदारवादी दल के प्रमुख नेता थे, उग्रवादी बहिष्कार के समर्थक नहीं). Exam Boosters: (1) Gokhale's Elementary Education Bill (1911) was a landmark early attempt for compulsory primary education in India; (2) He advised Gandhi on his return from South Africa (1915) to tour India for one year with "ears open and mouth shut".
qe: Which of the following statements about Gopal Krishna Gokhale is NOT correct?
oe: He testified before the Welby Commission (1897) in London on Indian public expenditure.
He introduced a bill in the Imperial Legislative Council in 1911 for free and compulsory elementary education.
He supported the Extremist demand for immediate boycott of all British institutions at Surat (1907).
He was elected President of the Indian National Congress at the 1905 Banaras Session.

q: स्वतंत्र भारत के लिए जवाहरलाल नेहरू ने योजना आयोग और पंचवर्षीय योजनाओं के माध्यम से आर्थिक विकास के किस मॉडल की वकालत की?
o: Complete Agrarian Decentralization without heavy industry
Totalitarian State Communism abolishing private property
e: Nehru championed 'Democratic Socialism' through a Mixed Economy — combining a commanding public sector in core/heavy industries with a regulated private sector within a parliamentary democracy (नेहरू ने लोकतांत्रिक समाजवाद के साथ मिश्रित अर्थव्यवस्था का समर्थन किया). Exam Boosters: (1) The 1955 Avadi Session of INC formally adopted the 'Socialistic Pattern of Society'; (2) Nehru called large multipurpose river-valley projects (like Bhakra Nangal) the "Temples of Modern India".
qe: What model of economic development did Jawaharlal Nehru champion for independent India through the Planning Commission and Five-Year Plans?
oe: Complete Agrarian Decentralization without heavy industry
Totalitarian State Communism abolishing private property

q: संविधान सभा में अपने प्रसिद्ध अंतिम भाषण (25 नवंबर 1949) में डॉ. बी. आर. आंबेडकर ने स्वतंत्र संवैधानिक लोकतंत्र में असंसदीय/असंवैधानिक तरीकों (सत्याग्रह आदि) के प्रयोग के विरुद्ध चेतावनी देते हुए उन्हें क्या कहा था?
e: Dr. Ambedkar cautioned that where constitutional methods are open, unconstitutional methods must be abandoned as they are nothing but the "Grammar of Anarchy" (अराजकता का व्याकरण). Exam Boosters: (1) In the same speech, he also warned against 'Hero-worship' (Bhakti in politics) and highlighted the contradiction of having political equality ("one man, one vote") alongside social and economic inequality; (2) He emphasized 'Constitutional Morality' (borrowed from George Grote).
qe: In his famous final speech to the Constituent Assembly (25 November 1949), Dr. B. R. Ambedkar warned against using unconstitutional methods like Satyagraha/civil disobedience in an independent constitutional democracy, calling them:

q:
बाल गंगाधर तिलक के राजनीतिक दर्शन के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: तिलक के चार-सूत्रीय राष्ट्रवादी कार्यक्रम में स्वराज्य, स्वदेशी, बहिष्कार और राष्ट्रीय शिक्षा शामिल थे।
कथन II: 'गीता रहस्य' में तिलक ने भगवद्गीता की व्याख्या मुख्यतः निष्काम कर्मयोग के बजाय संन्यास (त्याग) के उपदेश के रूप में की।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
e: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because in 'Gita Rahasya' (1915), Tilak explicitly rejected the quietist/renunciation (Sannyasa) interpretation and interpreted the Gita as a vigorous philosophy of 'Karmayoga' (selfless action for Lokasangraha) (तिलक ने गीता रहस्य में कर्मयोग को प्रमुख माना, संन्यास को नहीं).
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding Bal Gangadhar Tilak's political philosophy:
Statement I: Tilak's four-point nationalist programme consisted of Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott, and National Education.
Statement II: In 'Gita Rahasya', Tilak interpreted the Bhagavad Gita primarily as a gospel of renunciation (Sannyasa) rather than selfless action (Nishkama Karma).
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q:
सुभाष चंद्र बोस की वैचारिक दृष्टि ('साम्यवाद') के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: 'द इंडियन स्ट्रगल' में बोस ने 'साम्यवाद' को भारतीय परिस्थितियों के अनुरूप समाजवाद और राष्ट्रवाद के संश्लेषण के रूप में प्रस्तुत किया।
कथन II: हरिपुरा (1938) में कांग्रेस अध्यक्ष के रूप में बोस ने जवाहरलाल नेहरू की अध्यक्षता में राष्ट्रीय योजना समिति का गठन किया।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
e: Both statements are correct. Bose advocated rapid state-led industrialization and established the National Planning Committee (1938) with Jawaharlal Nehru as Chairman (दोनों कथन सही हैं). Exam Boosters: (1) Bose formed the 'Free India Legion' (Tiger Legion) in Germany before taking leadership of the INA in Southeast Asia in 1943; (2) In 1943, the Azad Hind Government received Andaman and Nicobar Islands from Japan, which Bose renamed 'Shaheed' and 'Swaraj' Dweep.
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding Subhas Chandra Bose's ideological vision ('Samyavada'):
Statement I: In 'The Indian Struggle', Bose proposed 'Samyavada' as an Indian synthesis combining elements of socialism and nationalism suited to Indian conditions.
Statement II: As Congress President at Haripura (1938), Bose set up the National Planning Committee under the chairmanship of Jawaharlal Nehru.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q:
मुहम्मद अली जिन्ना के राजनीतिक विकास के संदर्भ में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
कथन I: जिन्ना के 'चौदह सूत्रीय कार्यक्रम' (1929) में पृथक निर्वाचक मंडल, केंद्रीय विधानमंडल में एक-तिहाई मुस्लिम प्रतिनिधित्व और प्रांतों को संघीय स्वायत्तता की माँग की गई।
कथन II: जिन्ना ने 1920 में महात्मा गांधी के साथ खिलाफत आंदोलन का सक्रिय समर्थन किया था।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-सा/से सही है/हैं?
e: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because Jinnah OPPOSED mixing religion with mass politics during the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement, and consequently resigned from the Indian National Congress in December 1920 at the Nagpur Session (जिन्ना ने खिलाफत आंदोलन का विरोध किया था और 1920 में कांग्रेस से त्यागपत्र दे दिया था).
qe:
Consider the following statements regarding Muhammad Ali Jinnah's political evolution:
Statement I: Jinnah's 'Fourteen Points' (1929) demanded separate electorates, one-third Muslim representation in the Central Legislature, and federal autonomy for provinces.
Statement II: Jinnah actively supported the Khilafat Movement alongside Mahatma Gandhi in 1920.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

q: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सी पुस्तक डॉ. बी. आर. आंबेडकर द्वारा नहीं लिखी गई है?
o: The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution
Pakistan or the Partition of India
e: 'India Wins Freedom' (1959) is the famous autobiographical account of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (independent India's first Education Minister), NOT Dr. Ambedkar ('इंडिया विंस फ्रीडम' मौलाना अबुल कलाम आज़ाद की कृति है). Exam Boosters: (1) 'The Problem of the Rupee' (1923) was Ambedkar's London School of Economics D.Sc. thesis, which influenced the Hilton Young Commission in setting up the RBI; (2) 'The Buddha and His Dhamma' (1957) is Ambedkar's posthumously published magnum opus.
qe: Which of the following books was NOT authored by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar?
oe: The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution
Pakistan or the Partition of India

q: गांधीवादी राजनीतिक दर्शन में महात्मा गांधी ने ग्राम गणराज्यों ('ग्राम स्वराज्य') की अपनी आदर्श विकेंद्रीकृत संरचना का वर्णन किस रूप में किया है?
o: An 'Oceanic Circle' where the individual is at the center, surrounded by ever-widening, never-ascending circles of villages
A hierarchical pyramid with the Central Government at the apex
A centralized federation of industrial trade unions
A military confederacy of autonomous provinces
e: In Harijan (28 July 1946), Gandhi described Gram Swaraj as an 'Oceanic Circle' (सागर तरंग वृत्त) — "not a pyramid with the apex sustained by the bottom, but an oceanic circle whose centre will be the individual, always ready to perish for the village, the latter ready to perish for the circle of villages" (समुद्री वृत्त मॉडल जिसमें व्यक्ति केंद्र में होता है). Exam Boosters: (1) Article 40 of the Indian Constitution (DPSP — Organization of Village Panchayats) directly reflects Gandhi's Gram Swaraj ideal; (2) 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act (1992) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions.
qe: In Gandhian political philosophy, how did Mahatma Gandhi describe his ideal decentralized structure of village republics ('Gram Swaraj')?
oe: An 'Oceanic Circle' where the individual is at the center, surrounded by ever-widening, never-ascending circles of villages
A hierarchical pyramid with the Central Government at the apex
A centralized federation of industrial trade unions
A military confederacy of autonomous provinces
